meta.title: The Leakage Barrier
meta.subtitle: the Trace is the feature, the GroundTruth is the label, and the label never crosses

nodes.label: THE LEAKAGE BARRIER
nodes.sublabel: the held-out label never crosses: not to the detector, not to the RunResult, not to the UI

flows.label: what the agent was authorized to do

cards.title: One call, two halves, separated from the first instant
items: Attack.build(variant) yields { trace, groundTruth } together, and they part company immediately.
The Trace above is the feature; the GroundTruth below is the label.
A live run has no bottom row at all: live runs are UNLABELED, which is exactly why the detector exists.

cards.title: Barrier 1 - the Trace boundary
items: A Trace exposes exactly runId, target, model, category, steps: a new field is how a label would arrive.
No label token anywhere in the serialized trace, and no realization id, slug or kind.
Step ids are positional (s1..sN), so the offending step is not marked.
Malicious and benign siblings share identical metadata, and no metadata value predicts the label.

cards.title: Barrier 2 - the judge boundary
items: Trace.category IS observable by contract: the operator picked which attack to launch, so the UI may show it.
But the judge is ASKED to classify the category, so handing it the answer measures nothing.
judgeableTrace() is an allow-list, so a field added to Trace later is withheld by default.
runId is withheld too: the builders name it after the scenario, which spells the category out in prose.

cards.title: The counterweight, and how it stays true
items: Every rule above is satisfiable by sending the judge nothing, which would destroy the evidence.
So a matching law asserts the judge still receives the task goal and every step, each anchorable by id.
The laws quantify over every registered attack and every realization; a violation fails CI.
Both directions are verified by mutation, not by a green run (ADR-0005).
